A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–H are readable and support comparison, including the new Appendix A.4 in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix H report original numerical experiments on network training, approximation errors, parameter trajectories and potential-dependent implicit bias.

after.justification: V2 retains the original numerical experiments in Section 4 and Appendix H, including all nine experimental figures.

M1.justification: The shallow networks, squared-error objective, mirror-flow update and scaled-potential construction are retained. V2 expands theoretical guarantees for multivariate models and uncentered potentials; these constructions were already discussed in v1 Appendices D and E.2, rather than being new optimization procedures.

E1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix G use the same synthetic univariate regression datasets and vertically shifted labels. The broader multivariate theory is not accompanied by multivariate experiments.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same quadratic-potential/gradient-descent, spline and variational-solution comparisons. No comparator is added or removed from Figures 1–9.

E3.justification: Appendix G retains full-batch training, the potential-specific learning rates, the 10^-7 loss threshold, the 501-point discretization and the same error metrics. The experimental network configurations are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H retains the same analyses of parameter trajectories, lazy versus kernel behavior, potential sensitivity, hypentropy and network width. No ablation or supplementary experimental analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five training repetitions with different random initializations for the middle panels of Figures 1 and 2. The plotted error bars and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All nine experimental figure graphics are identical across versions. The reported approximation trends, training trajectories and potential-dependent curvature findings are retained without added, removed or revised empirical results.

T1.justification: Theorems 2 and 9 in v2 extend training-dynamics guarantees to general input dimension, with corresponding changes to Appendix A/B proofs and parameter-space results. New Appendix A.4 adds Assumption 25 and Theorem 26, with a proof sketch extending the unscaled results to uncentered potentials under bounded bias initialization. The explicit univariate variational characterizations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.1 broaden the claimed lazy-training results and unscaled gradient-flow equivalence beyond univariate inputs. They explicitly distinguish these general-dimensional guarantees from the retained univariate function-space characterizations, substantially expanding the claimed theoretical applicability.

C2.justification: The conclusion now identifies the variational characterization specifically as univariate, rather than describing the entire analysis that way. Remark 3 explains when centering can be dropped, and Section 4 clarifies how Gaussian initialization concentrates curvature near the origin in the existing Figure 2.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement replaces the anonymous code-repository location with the author's GitHub repository. Appendix G retains the same implementation, learning-rate, discretization and software-version details.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 revises representation-cost positioning to acknowledge established connections with implicit bias and distinguish prior L1 costs from this work's L2/Bregman costs. It adds Gunasekar et al. (2018b) and Boursier and Flammarion (2023), and removes Jacot et al. (2022).

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Mirror Descent' to 'Mirror Flow', affiliations are shortened, and the related-work paragraph, proof roadmap and experimental explanation receive localized edits. Appendix A.4 is inserted while the overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: The author block becomes more compact, Figure 1 moves from page 10 to page 9, and appendix figures are repositioned relative to their discussion. The nine plot graphics, axes and legends remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 usefully broadens the dynamics analysis beyond univariate inputs and supplies an argument for dropping potential centering under bounded bias initialization. Clearer applicability boundaries and revised research positioning also improve the paper. These gains are limited relative to the central contribution: the explicit univariate variational characterizations and all empirical validation remain unchanged.
